prompt: ECMAScript IsTypedArrayOutOfBounds zero-length ByteOffset equals bufferByteLength
answer:
When `O.[[ByteOffset]] == bufferByteLength`, `IsTypedArrayOutOfBounds` returns **false**, including for a zero-length TypedArray.

The algorithm returns `true` only if:

```text
byteOffsetStart > bufferByteLength
or
byteOffsetEnd > bufferByteLength
```

It explicitly notes that zero-length TypedArrays are not considered out of bounds. Therefore, a TypedArray whose offset is exactly at the end of the buffer is zero-length but **not OOB**. A detached buffer is the exception: it is considered out of bounds. ([spec result](https://github.com/tc39/proposal-resizablearraybuffer/blob/master/spec.html); [implementation](https://github.com/LadybirdBrowser/ladybird/blob/abfd5ab8/Libraries/LibJS/Runtime/TypedArray.cpp))
